subject: Retention handoff for Greenbank migration — restore window & deletion propagation
messages:
From: Markus Jensen <markus@greenbank.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@greenbank.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: DR retention & deletion propagation questions for migration

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. As we scope the cutover to Redwood Private I need to confirm a few DR/backup behaviors so our infra and legal teams can sign off:

- When a user request to delete data is accepted by the control plane, how long until all offline backups and cross-region replicas are fully expunged? We have to map this against our 72-hour incident SLA and a possible 30-day legal hold.
- Are there distinct timelines for: control-plane metadata erasure, primary datastore tombstoning, offsite snapshot purge, and any longer-term cold-archive retention? Please provide realistic upper bounds.
- During a legal hold, can we prevent snapshot sweep jobs for a specified account? If so, what is the API/ops process you recommend so we don't inadvertently trigger asynchronous archive sweeps?

We've attached a short list of our DR requirements and the legal-hold template. Can you confirm by EOD Monday so we can circulate internally?

Thanks,
Markus
IT Operations — Greenbank

Attachments: greenbank_drp_requirements.pdf, legal-hold-instructions.docx

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Jensen <markus@greenbank.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DR retention & deletion propagation questions for migration

Markus — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Monica (Security & Compliance) and Aditya (Platform) so we can give both operational windows and compliance controls. Quick summary up front, then proposed next steps below.

Summary (high level expectations):
- Control-plane metadata removal: near-immediate (seconds to minutes) from the account index; this is the user-visible deletion.
- Primary datastore tombstone + compaction: visible tombstones are written synchronously; compaction/physical data reclamation can take up to 48 hours depending on active write load and shard rebuilds.
- Geo-replica propagation: async replication + tombstone convergence — up to 72 hours in worst-case cross-region failover scenarios.
- Snapshot/offsite purge: snapshots are marked for purge at expiry; sweep jobs run on a daily window and actual object-level deletion (cold archive purge) can take up to 30 days after the snapshot expiry date.

Notes/nuance:
- We separate logical deletion (control-plane removal + tenant metadata) from physical expunge (object-level removal from cold storage). For compliance mapping you should treat the physical expunge window as the conservative bound (control plane may show deletion earlier).
- If an account is placed on legal hold, offsite sweep jobs observe an account-level hold tag. That prevents the snapshot from being queued for purge; it also prevents the purge worker from removing objects until the tag is cleared. The hold is applied via a simple API call or via Console (we'll share both).
- There are two additional edge cases to be aware of: 1) restore window after a snapshot purge may be impossible for objects already reclaimed from cold storage; 2) if you use cross-region replication with custom retention overrides there can be additional tenant-specific delays while we reconcile retention tags.

Proposed next steps:
1) Monica to provide SOC2 / audit evidence pointers (audit-log exports and retention-tagging proof).
2) Aditya to propose the exact API call and Console steps to set an account-level legal hold and the RBAC requirements.
3) We schedule a 30-minute sync early next week with Greenbank legal to confirm the hold lifecycle and sign-off on restore SLAs.

Action items for you: please confirm whether you need the conservative "physical expunge" windows (30-day offsite purge) documented in your internal runbook, or if you want us to provide a tailored statement of expected data visibility for customer-facing docs.

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Jensen <markus@greenbank.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DR retention & deletion propagation questions for migration

Markus — thanks, this is the right set of questions. A few compliance-specific clarifications and evidence we can supply: 

- Audit logs: we can export time-indexed logs showing deletion API calls, retention-tag changes, and the snapshot sweep job events. These are available in CSV/JSON and we can provision a filtered dump for your legal team.
- Legal holds: we support an "account_hold" tag that is honored by the daily purge worker. Applying the hold requires an admin API key (we'll provide a scoped service account); removal is also auditable.
- E-Discovery: if Greenbank needs a forensically-signed archive for litigation, we can perform a one-off export and notarize the export with a signed manifest — this is billed as a professional-services engagement.

Evidence we will attach to the call (we'll upload to your Drive link):
- A sample audit log extract showing a deletion + sweep job pause
- Documentation for the API to set/clear account_hold
- A short runbook for on-call ops to safely run manual purges for an account (advice on concurrency, shard drain, and verification checks)

Two practical asks from Greenbank legal:
1) Please confirm whether you want the automated daily sweep window (we default to a rolling midnight UTC job) changed to a fixed-windows approach during your migration cutover. If yes, we'll schedule a controlled freeze.
2) Please supply the legal-hold email alias you'll use so we can whitelist it for programmatic hold requests (we recommend legal@greenbank.com).

I'll be available for a call Monday morning PST.

—Monica
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
